name: WebinarIgnition – Live, Automated & Evergreen Webinar System for WordPress and WooCommerce
author: Tobias @Saleswonder.biz

sections.description:
Run live, automated, and evergreen webinars on WordPress — registration, reminders, and sales on your own site. Free unlimited webinars; WooCommerce checkout inside the room on Plus.

  • Unlimited live, automated, and evergreen webinars — free on WordPress.org
  • Unlimited attendees; AI wizard for registration pages and reminder emails (24 languages)
  • Registration forms anywhere — footer, sidebar, popup (shortcodes)
  • Automated reminder emails — confirmation through post-webinar follow-up
  • WooCommerce-ready — button CTA on Free; checkout inside the webinar room on Plus
  • Works with YouTube Live, Zoom, Vimeo, or your own stream — optional built-in live video on Plus
  • Per-webinar language, timezone, and date format
  • 30-day Plus trial inside the plugin — unlock leads, unlimited CTAs, and in-room checkout

Quick start: 13-video setup playlist · AI content wizard · live demo webinars below

Who is this for?

  • WooCommerce shop owners who want to sell during the webinar, not after everyone leaves
  • Course creators and coaches who need registration, reminders, and evergreen replays in one plugin
  • Agencies running multilingual campaigns for clients
  • EU/DACH hosts who need GDPR-friendly registration and streaming on their own WordPress site

How pricing works (no surprises)

Free runs forever — unlimited live, automated, and evergreen webinars with unlimited attendees, no time limit, no demo mode. There are no per-attendee fees and no seat tiers: your price never jumps because one webinar did unusually well. Other platforms lock you into a high monthly tier all year even if you only fill the room once.

Plus ($99/mo) is for when you want to sell inside the room (WooCommerce and other checkouts), need built-in live video, and unlock individual leads and automations. Same flat plugin price whether you host a small group or a packed session — you only pay for the streaming you actually use.

Free (install from WordPress.org)

For: test and run real webinars before you pay.

  • Unlimited live, automated, and evergreen webinars
  • Unlimited attendees — dashboard shows total sign-up count
  • AI content wizard — registration pages and reminder emails (24 languages)
  • One in-webinar action per event — polls, booking, or any WordPress shortcode
  • Registration forms anywhere — footer, sidebar, popup (shortcodes)
  • Automated reminder emails — fully customizable
  • Per-webinar language, timezone, and date format
  • WooCommerce button CTA — link to your shop (checkout opens in a new tab)
  • 30-day Plus trial available inside the plugin

Unlimited plan

For: solo creators who never want to hit limits.

All paid plans include unlimited registrations, attendees, webinar time, webinars, and in-webinar interactions — extend with any WordPress plugin (polls, forms, booking, …).

  • Everything in Free, plus unlimited in-webinar interactions per event
  • Individual lead details — name, email, attendance, custom fields
  • Send registration and attendance data to your CRM (ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp, KlickTipp, FluentCRM, and more)
  • Paid webinars — charge for access (WooCommerce, Stripe, PayPal, Digistore24)
  • Bulk lead import and export (CSV)
  • 1:1 consultant tech support

Plus plan

For: growing teams who want more sales from every webinar.

  • Everything in Unlimited, plus:
  • Webinar grid — visitors find live and evergreen offers fast
  • Built-in live video (100ms) — meet and stream in a focused room (up to 20,000 viewers)
  • External page CTAs inside the webinar — checkout or booking pages as live offers
  • WooCommerce checkout inside the webinar room — no redirect, sell while trust is warm
  • 1:1 technical done-for-you setup

Plus VIP plan

For: hands-on VIP support and email automation bundled.

  • Everything in Plus, plus:
  • 1:1 VIP technical support — direct line to an expert
  • VIP meetings — plan funnels and launches together
  • Groundhogg Pro (1 site) included — email automation on your server

See all plans: webinarignition.com/#pricing

Real hosts, real results

Melanie needed registration, reminders, and tracking connected on WordPress — not five plugins that do not talk to each other. Tom stopped selling on the landing page and filled live webinars instead; by the third session, trust did the selling. Bastian demoed leather craft live and opened WooCommerce checkout inside the room so buyers never lost momentum.

Felix ran a symposium, not a sales pitch.

Seven hours live — 19 May 2026, 10:00–17:00 CET.
German and English, with live translation and language switching inside the webinar room.
About 600 people registered. More than 100 questions asked and answered in two-way chat — directly in the room, not in a separate tool.

The stream ran through 3Q Video — GDPR/DSGVO-compliant hosting in Germany and Europe, not a US-only stack.
Registrations, calendar entries, and reminder emails: all on WebinarIgnition, on 14a.tv.

Same live room you already know — cleaned up and ready for large crowds.
During the event, our live-update service (hosted in Frankfurt) sends instant signals to every screen — a new CTA, a new question, your answer, a status change — so your WordPress site does not have to reload over and over.
All registrations, chat, and attendee data stay on your WordPress site, where your hosting already is. The helper does not store that data.
Available on every plan, including free.

New: AI Webinar Content Wizard

You probably don’t wake up in the morning excited to write registration copy and reminder emails.

The AI wizard is there for exactly that.
Answer three simple questions — what your webinar is about, who it is for, and what should happen afterwards.
From there, the wizard creates three registration page versions and four reminder emails in your language.

24 languages included. More on request. Best quality powered by AI.

You don’t lose control. You can read, adjust and translate every line.
But you never have to start from a blank page again.

Generate your first webinar content here

Step-by-step setup playlist (13 videos, AI in video 3): Watch on YouTube

Free: AI Connector (MCP)

Connect an AI assistant — Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP-capable tools — to your WordPress site, and build webinars from that chat.

What you can do from the chat:

  • Ask whether WebinarIgnition fits and what it costs — “Does WebinarIgnition fit what I need? What does it cost, and which integrations does it support?”
  • Find a topic and create the webinar — “I run a dog school. Find a topic for my audience and write my webinar — title, invitation emails and registration page.”
  • Set up and change the webinar on your own WordPress — “Set up my webinar on https://my-site.com and move the start date to next Tuesday.”

The assistant can create and update webinars: registration pages, emails, dates, and settings. You read and edit every line afterwards, the same way as with the AI wizard above. What an assistant can do depends on the assistant and its plan.

It works on ordinary hosting, and it also works when your site cannot be reached from outside — behind a bot wall, a firewall, or shared hosting that blocks incoming requests. The site then reaches the connector itself and polls for work: no inbound access is needed, and nothing on your host has to change.

You find it under WebinarIgnition > AI connection (the same connection panel is on the Settings screen). Connecting needs an administrator account. Free on every plan.

Join a live demo webinar

  • Webinar Driver School (English): Beginner to pro — all welcome — Thursday 11:15 a.m. Panama time (UTC-5, 16:15 UTC)
  • WooCommerce Shop Owners: Triple Your WooCommerce Sales in 30 Minutes
  • WooCommerce Agencies: Stop starting every client project from zero
  • German (DE): Wednesday 18:30 Berlin time (CET)
  • Demo site: demo.webinarignition.com

Free Webinar Plugin for WooCommerce

Install from WordPress.org and run complete webinars before you pay — live, automated, and evergreen, with unlimited events and attendees. See the Free (install from WordPress.org) plan block above for the full list.

Start free, run a few webinars, and upgrade when you need individual lead details, unlimited in-room actions, CRM handoff, or WooCommerce checkout inside the room. Plans: webinarignition.com/#pricing

Paid Plans: WooCommerce Shops, Agencies & Creators

See the Unlimited, Plus, and Plus VIP plan blocks at the top of this page for the full feature list. All paid plans include unlimited registrations, attendees, webinar time, webinars, and in-webinar interactions.

See all plans: webinarignition.com/#pricing

What Only WebinarIgnition Does

  • WooCommerce checkout embedded inside the webinar room — no redirect, auto-fill customer data, sell while the feeling is warm (Plus)
  • AI-generated registration pages + reminder emails — 3 pages, 4 emails, 24 languages, in minutes (free on all plans)
  • Registration shortcodes anywhere, unlimited times — footer, sidebar, popup, any page
  • Per-webinar language, timezone, and date format — your attendees register and buy in their native language
  • 24 languages out of the box — every language on request, best quality by AI
  • Recurring live webinars + re-invite all registered with one click
  • 1-click registration from email — attendees click once, instantly registered, no form fill
  • Custom registration fields auto-filled in CTAs and CRM handoff (paid plans)
  • 100ms live video — up to 20,000 participants (Plus)
  • All webinar types in one plugin — live, automated, evergreen, no add-ons needed
  • No attendee limits on any plan

WooCommerce Integration

  • Free: Add a button CTA linking to your WooCommerce product page — keep the connection warm, send them to the shop when the moment is right
  • Plus: Embed WooCommerce checkout directly inside the webinar room — products, subscriptions, upsells without a page redirect, while trust is at its peak
  • Auto-fill checkout forms with data from webinar registration (name, email, address for logged-in customers)
  • Sell WooCommerce subscriptions, memberships, and courses inside webinars
  • Integrate with CartFlows, FunnelKit, and WPFunnels for complete funnel automation
  • Send registration and attendance data (name, email, campaign tags, attended status, product purchased) to your CRM

Integrations

  • Email & CRM: ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp, Mautic, KlickTipp, FluentCRM, Groundhogg, Brevo — via webhooks or direct
  • Payments: WooCommerce, Digistore24, Stripe, PayPal
  • Upsell funnels: CartFlows, FunnelKit, WPFunnels
  • Video: YouTube Live, Zoom, Vimeo, your own live stream, MP4/video files, iframe embeds; built-in live video (100ms) on Plus
  • Social login: Nextend Social Login (22+ providers, external, free or ~$50)
  • Page builders: Elementor, Gutenberg/FSE, Divi, Beaver Builder, Thrive Architect, Oxygen, Bricks

Multilingual Webinars — 24 Languages

Your webinar works best when people can follow every line without effort.
Reading and listening in a second language always costs energy — and every bit of extra effort lowers conversion.

Each webinar runs in its own language, timezone and date format.
Registration page, emails, thank-you page and the webinar room itself adapt to the audience you choose.

24 languages out of the box. Every language on request. Best quality powered by AI.

Hand-translated: English (en_US), German (de_DE)
AI-translated: Spanish (es_ES, es_MX), French (fr_FR), Italian (it_IT), Dutch (nl_NL), Portuguese (pt_BR, pt_PT), Russian (ru_RU), Chinese (zh_CN), Hindi (hi_IN), Turkish (tr_TR), Ukrainian (uk), Hungarian (hu_HU), Croatian (hr), Japanese (ja), Urdu (ur), Bulgarian (bg), Romanian (ro)

Add or refine translations with the free Loco Translate plugin (auto-translate via DeepL, Microsoft, ChatGPT built in).

GDPR & Privacy

All registration and attendee data stays on your own server. Double opt-in is required before any contact is saved as a participant. Forms include consent fields and compliance options for EU/DACH. No participant data is sent to external services without your explicit configuration.
sections.installation:
1. Install via Plugins > Add New > WebinarIgnition, or upload the zip file
  2. Activate the plugin
  3. Open the WebinarIgnition dashboard and follow the quick-start video playlist (13 videos)
  4. Create your first webinar — the AI wizard generates your registration page and reminder emails in minutes
  5. Use registration shortcodes to embed the sign-up form anywhere on your site
  6. Configure email delivery — WordPress wp_mail() works out of the box; install an SMTP plugin (e.g. SureMail) for reliable deliverability
  7. Optionally start the 30-day Ultimate Plus trial from inside the plugin to unlock in-room checkout, multiple CTAs, webhooks, and full lead management

Optional:
– Install Nextend Social Login for social registration (free or ~$50 once)
– Book a free onboarding call: webinarignition.com/meet-us
sections.faq:
What is the best free webinar plugin for WooCommerce?

WebinarIgnition is the only free webinar plugin built specifically for WooCommerce. The free version includes unlimited live, automated, and evergreen webinars with unlimited attendees, AI-generated registration pages, and one in-webinar interaction per event. No attendee limits, no demo mode, no time restriction. When you are ready to sell inside the webinar room, the Plus plan adds WooCommerce in-room checkout — no redirect, auto-fill customer data, close the sale while trust is at its peak.

Is there a free alternative to WebinarNinja, Demio, or EasyWebinar on WordPress?

Yes. WebinarIgnition runs entirely on your own site — no monthly SaaS platform, no attendee limits, no data leaving your server. The free version covers live, automated, and evergreen webinars with registration, reminders, and one in-webinar action. Paid plans add in-room WooCommerce checkout, webhooks, unlimited CTAs, and 100ms live video for up to 20,000 participants. You own everything: your leads, your recordings, your funnel.

What is the best WordPress plugin for webinars with WooCommerce?

WebinarIgnition is the only webinar plugin that embeds WooCommerce checkout directly inside the webinar room — no redirect, no drop-off. Attendees buy during the webinar without leaving. Auto-fill pre-populates checkout with registration data and existing WooCommerce customer details. The free version adds a button CTA linking to your WooCommerce product page. In-room checkout is available on the Plus plan.

What does the free version include — and what is in the paid plans?

Run complete webinars from day one — unlimited events, unlimited attendees, AI-generated registration pages, and one in-webinar interaction per event. No demo mode, no time limit. Free shows the total sign-up count in your dashboard; individual lead details and CRM handoff require Unlimited or a Plus trial.

See the plan blocks at the top of this page: Free, Unlimited, Plus, and Plus VIP. Full pricing: webinarignition.com/#pricing

Can I run live, automated, and evergreen webinars with one plugin?

Yes. WebinarIgnition handles all three webinar types in a single plugin. All types share the same engine: CTAs, polls, booking forms, and checkout appear identically whether live or automated. The free version includes all three types with unlimited events and attendees.

How does the AI webinar content generator work?

Answer 3 questions about your webinar and add your website URL. The AI wizard generates 3 conversion-ready registration page layouts and 4 reminder emails in your language. 24 languages included, more on request, best quality powered by AI. Available on all plans including free. Quick Start guide

Is WebinarIgnition optimized for AI search (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews)?

Yes. WebinarIgnition uses structured data, clear semantic markup, and explicit feature descriptions that AI assistants can easily parse and cite. The plugin FAQ, feature pages, and documentation are written to answer the specific questions AI assistants are asked about webinar solutions for WordPress.

How is WebinarIgnition different from WebinarPress?

WebinarIgnition is built around WooCommerce-first sales automation and multilingual audiences. WebinarPress focuses on English-only general lead generation. Key differences:

  • Multilingual: WebinarIgnition supports 24 languages per-webinar — registration pages, emails, thank-you pages, and the webinar room all adapt automatically. Your attendees register and convert in their native language. WebinarPress is English only — non-native speakers take longer to understand your offer, and non-localized webinars convert less.
  • In-room checkout: WebinarIgnition embeds WooCommerce checkout inside the webinar (Plus). WebinarPress redirects to a product page.
  • AI content: WebinarIgnition generates registration pages and reminder emails in 24 languages on all plans. WebinarPress has no AI content wizard.
  • Evergreen in free: WebinarIgnition includes automated and evergreen webinars in the free version. WebinarPress locks automated webinars to Pro.
  • Shortcodes anywhere: Registration forms work in footers, sidebars, and popups, unlimited times on the same page. WebinarPress shortcodes are page-only.
  • 1-click registration: WebinarIgnition sends personalized one-click registration links via email. WebinarPress does not.
  • 100ms live video: Built-in 100ms video for up to 20,000 participants (Plus). WebinarPress relies on external Zoom/YouTube.
  • Active development: WebinarIgnition ships major features regularly (see changelog). WebinarPress releases are mostly security patches since 2022.

Can I embed the registration form in my website footer, sidebar, or popup?

Yes. Since version 4.08, registration shortcodes work anywhere — footers, sidebars, widgets, popups, and multiple times on the same page. The shortcode inherits your theme’s colors and fonts automatically.

How do recurring live webinars work?

Create a live webinar and set it to recur weekly, bi-weekly, or on a custom schedule. After each session, re-invite all previously registered attendees with one click — they receive a new 1-click registration link without re-entering their details.

Can I use custom registration fields inside the webinar or in webhooks?

Yes. Fields like participant reason, UTM parameters, and any custom fields are available in CTAs, email templates, and webhook payloads (paid plans). This enables advanced segmentation: “registered with reason: product demo AND attended AND did not buy.”

Does WebinarIgnition support paid webinars?

Yes. Charge for access via WooCommerce, Stripe, PayPal, or Digistore24. Attendees purchase the webinar and receive a secure access link automatically. Available on the Unlimited plan and above.

What video sources are supported?

YouTube Live, Zoom, Vimeo Live, any RTMP stream, MP4/video files, iframes, and the built-in 100ms live video infrastructure (up to 20,000 participants, Plus plan). Set a different video source per webinar.

Can I automate a complete sales funnel with WebinarIgnition?

Yes. Set up an evergreen webinar with timed CTAs, connect webhooks to your email tool, and trigger sequences based on attendance status. Use 1-click registration links in emails for frictionless re-entry. Combine with CartFlows or FunnelKit for WooCommerce upsell sequences. Full funnel: opt-in -> webinar -> in-room offer -> post-webinar follow-up.

Can each webinar be in a different language and timezone?

Yes. Every webinar has its own language, timezone, and date/time format. 24 languages included. Every language on request. Best quality powered by AI. Ideal for agencies running multilingual campaigns or global audiences.

What email reminders are included?

All plans include: registration confirmation, 1 day before, 1 hour before, when live, and after the webinar — all fully customizable. On paid plans, send registration data via webhooks to trigger advanced automations like “registered but did not attend.”

Is WebinarIgnition GDPR-compliant?

Yes. All data stays on your own server. Double opt-in is enforced before any contact is added as a participant. Full compliance options for EU/DACH.

What is the done-for-you setup service?

Available on the Plus plan: our team personally configures your email delivery, email marketing connection, video source, streaming provider, and registration page design. Goal: your first webinar goes live with 100% tech success. Unlimited includes 1:1 consultant tech support; Plus VIP adds VIP support and VIP planning meetings.

Can I report security bugs?

Yes. Report through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program.

EXTERNAL SERVICES

This plugin may connect to external services depending on your configuration:

  • Freemius: licensing, updates, and trial management (freemius.com/privacy) — required
  • 100ms Video Meetings: built-in live video, Plus plans only (100ms.live/privacy-policy) — optional
  • Google APIs: Calendar, YouTube Live, Google Meet (Google privacy policy) — optional
  • Stripe: payment processing (stripe.com/privacy) — optional
  • Nextend Social Login: social registration, 22+ providers, external plugin — optional
  • WebinarIgnition AI relay: powers the built-in AI content wizard / AI Agent, optional — only used when you actively use the AI wizard ([WebinarIgnition privacy policy](CLARIFY: Tobias to supply final Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs for the WI AI relay))
  • CDN resources: Bootstrap, Video.js, jQuery, Moment.js, Luxon

About the AI content wizard / AI Agent (optional): When — and only when — you use the AI wizard or AI Agent inside wp-admin to draft a webinar, registration page, or reminder emails, the plugin sends your request to the WebinarIgnition AI relay (hosted on Fly.io, default endpoint https://wi-node-ai-relay.fly.dev), which forwards it to an AI model provider (Anthropic Claude; Perplexity is used for web-research tasks). What is sent: the text you type, the structured webinar concept you build in the wizard (goal, audience, topic, title, tone, speaker/guest names, key points and notes, video URLs, schedule), your WordPress site domain and site URL, plugin version, license plan, and your own WordPress profile display name and bio (used to personalize copy). No attendee, registrant, or lead data (participant names, emails, chat messages) is sent to the AI relay. Why: to generate the webinar copy, pages, and emails you asked the wizard to write. The API keys live on the relay, never in your WordPress install. The AI writing and conversation guidance itself (the prompt instructions that make the copy good) is served by the relay as part of that same service and is not stored inside the plugin; the plugin keeps only a short offline fallback so the free build stays usable without it. This is entirely optional: all core webinar features — registration, reminders, live room, replay, WooCommerce CTAs — work without the AI wizard, and the free WordPress.org build runs standalone without it. AI provider policies: Anthropic privacy policy, Perplexity privacy policy. WebinarIgnition AI relay Terms of Service and Privacy Policy: CLARIFY — Tobias to supply final URLs.

No participant data is sent to any external service without your explicit configuration.

DOMAIN USAGE DISCLOSURE

WebinarIgnition may connect to: freemius.com (required), 100ms.live (optional), googleapis.com (optional), stripe.com (optional), social login provider domains (optional), wi-node-ai-relay.fly.dev (optional — AI content wizard / AI Agent only; forwards to api.anthropic.com and api.perplexity.ai), CDN domains for Bootstrap, Video.js, jQuery, Moment.js, Luxon.
sections.changelog:
4.24.0 — 14 October 2026

Changing a date no longer re-writes your texts. Telling the agent “move it to the 15th” used to run the full copy writer behind the scenes, so approved wording could be overwritten even though you only touched the date. The date, the time and the time zone are now written on their own — your registration page, your e-mails and the room follow immediately, and every text stays exactly as you wrote it.

You see what a changed fact touches, and you decide what gets re-written. The moment a fact changes, the agent names the places it shows up in and offers “Re-write the texts”. Tapping it opens a short checklist (registration page texts, e-mails) — nothing is written until you pick and confirm. A full run in the background is over.

A note you told the agent can be removed or reworded. Notes used to be add-only, so a fact that had become wrong stayed in the list forever. The line you name can now be replaced or struck, one line at a time.

The privacy line under the sign-up form can be changed. It was fixed interface text with no way in; it is a normal participant line now, changeable per webinar.

Only the marked part of a line changes. Marking a phrase inside a sentence — or asking for a dot or a line break after a word — used to rewrite the whole block and could swallow the sentence next to it.

Earlier versions can be restored — several steps, not just one. Page versions come from WordPress’ own revisions, settings like the title or the date from the agent’s own history. The list is readable: time, who changed it, and the text that changed.

The thank-you page’s date is checked. If it carries the date as fixed text and that text no longer matches the webinar’s date, the agent says so and offers to repair the page.

4.20.86 — 5 October 2026

Rendering and cache fixes for the participant path. A room or registration page could show stale content after a deploy; the page cache is now bypassed correctly for the participant surfaces. Internal clean-up, nothing to configure.

4.20.81 — 3 October 2026

The agent can change one line of text without re-writing the whole webinar. A host who wanted one sentence replaced got the whole block re-written instead, losing the wording he had approved. A change now replaces exactly the addressed line.

4.20.69 — 2 October 2026

A webinar now shows the money that really came in, with the open orders in brackets. Until now only paid orders (processing/completed) counted. A prepayment or an unpaid order sat at “pending”/”on-hold” and showed nothing. The sale line now names two worths: the paid sum stands large and first, the open orders follow in brackets (“1 purchase · 99.00 € (2 open · 398.00 €)”). When an order is later paid, a follow-up over the next month moves it from the bracket into the paid sum — the order is never counted twice. A refund subtracts as before.

The account coupling now requires the real mail click. A purchase is only attached to an existing customer account when the lead actually opened the confirmation link from the mailed registration — not merely by filling in the form.

4.20.68 — 2 October 2026

Switching an existing webinar to another language now also rewrites its standard form labels. Setting the participant language used to change only the stored language, so a registration page that was created in German kept the German standard labels (registration button, short mobile label, name and email placeholders) on an English webinar. The switch now rewrites exactly those labels that still carry the old language’s default text, drawn from the plugin’s own translations. A label the host typed himself is never overwritten; it is named back in the result instead. The time zone is now set on live webinars as well.

4.20.67 — 2 October 2026

The account protection in the Block checkout now really runs, and it also covers the shipping address. When a returning customer’s order is attached to their account, WebinarIgnition copies the saved address beforehand and restores it after WooCommerce’s own customer sync, so a quick guest form cannot blank it. That copy is now taken on the hook WooCommerce actually calls, and it saves the billing and shipping address alike.

The checkout hint appears in the classic checkout. The small “you already have an account” hint above the checkout form is shown in the classic (shortcode) checkout. The earlier note that it also appears in the Block checkout was not correct and has been removed.

4.20.66 — 2 October 2026

A returning customer’s order now lands in their own account, not as a guest order.

If someone registered for your webinar and already has a shop account, their purchase used to
arrive as a guest order under the same email address. It worked, but it never showed up in their
account, and they were never asked whether they already have one. When the purchase carries a
valid webinar token, the order is now attached to that existing account. No login is needed and
the customer sees no extra step. Without the token nothing changes, so a checkout that did not
come from your webinar behaves exactly as before.

Checkout now tells a returning customer that they can log in. A small hint appears above the
checkout form when the visitor comes from your webinar and already has an account. It is our own
text and stays visible.

4.20.65 — 2 October 2026

This is the same feature set as 4.20.64; only the version number is new. It exists so this beta build has a number of its own for the Freemius re-upload: 4.20.64 was already the live build on the server, and Freemius held that version as uploaded without publishing it. Nothing about your webinars changes.

4.20.64 — 2 October 2026

The AI assistant no longer hides behind the WordPress admin menu in focus mode. When focus mode took over the screen, the assistant panel sat at the very left edge (x=0) and slipped underneath the admin menu — on wide screens and on narrow ones alike. It now follows the menu the way every other WordPress admin page does: 160px with the menu open, 36px when the menu is collapsed, and 0px on narrow screens where the menu becomes a drawer.

4.20.62 — 2 October 2026

This is the same feature set as 4.20.61; only the version number is new. It exists so this test build has a number of its own: 4.20.61 was never offered as a download, and 4.20.59 was the last version on the server. Nothing about your webinars changes.

4.20.61 — 2 October 2026

An elopage checkout that goes out as a button now carries the buyer’s name and e-mail. 4.20.57 established, measured, that an elopage/ablefy checkout must not be framed (its session cookie does not survive the frame) — so it goes out as a button. It turned out the button was leaving value on the table: measured on a real public checkout (GET only, nothing submitted, nothing bought, and confirmed inside a real frame) elopage fills first_name, last_name and email server-side into the form’s own fields, and ?locale=de switches the order form’s language. Exactly those three fill; phone, salutation, payer_email, full_name, name and invented names fill nothing, and the checkout shows neither a phone nor a salutation field at all — so nothing else is appended. The provider row now holds the three measured parameters, the two domains elopage.com and myablefy.com are recognised, and the offer panel’s warning names the button route with its prefill instead of only the refusal.

And the provider you already know is no longer thrown away. An elopage checkout may run on the host’s own domain (…/s/<shop>/<product>/payment), where a host lookup can never recognise it — the offer lost its prefill although the console knew the provider. The analysis now accepts the provider the caller already resolved whenever the host lookup finds nothing; an unknown provider is still never invented, and a link from a provider with no documented parameters still goes out byte-identical.

The “Checked addresses” list under the link check now names the real reason too. 4.20.59 fixed the single sentence, but the list still read “answers, but refuses to be embedded” for a table-measured checkout such as elopage — the page does render there, only the purchase breaks on the provider’s session cookie. The list now shows the same measured sentence whenever the provider table decided the “no”; a live “no” and every other state keep their text word for word. Rows saved before this version (without the source field) keep the previous text as well.

4.20.59 — 2 October 2026

The link check in the console now reads the provider table too, so the host reads the real reason a checkout stays a button. The live check can only read what the address itself answers; for elopage that answer carries no framing headers, so it said “embedding not confirmed” even though the table has held a measured “no” since 4.20.57. The check now asks the table whenever the live answer is “unknown”: a table “no” is taken with its measured reason, a live “no” or “yes” still wins unchanged, and a table “yes” never becomes a recommendation (an unproven frame is not offered). The three existing sentences are unchanged; the measured case gets its own — “the provider’s session cookie does not survive the frame”.

4.20.58 — 2 October 2026

The offer panel now names the real reason a checkout stays a button. A checkout can end up as a button for two different reasons: the address itself refuses to be embedded, or it allows the frame while the purchase breaks on the provider’s session cookie (measured for elopage). Both were described with the same sentence, “does not allow being embedded” — which is untrue for the second case. The line now says which of the two was actually found, and the live check always wins: when the address itself refuses the frame, that sentence stays exactly as it was.

4.20.57 — 2 October 2026

An elopage checkout is a button, for a measured reason. Three public elopage/ablefy checkouts were checked: none of them sends X-Frame-Options or a frame-ancestors directive, so the page itself would render — but the session cookie p_user-session-id is set without SameSite=None; Secure, so inside the webinar frame the browser does not send it and the purchase cannot be completed. Offering the frame would show the buyer a working order form and break at the moment he pays. The provider row therefore no longer reads “not proven” but a measured “no”, and the host reads that measured reason instead of a generic line.

4.20.56 — 1 October 2026

Texts now follow your language, with English as the fallback. The AI Agent and the wizard answered in German while the source texts are English, because six places read the language from the request and fell back to German, and the language instruction sat far up in the prompt between German examples. The language now follows what the host sends, then the browser’s own signal, and only then English; the instruction sits at the end of the prompt where it is read. Nothing to configure.

4.20.55 — 1 October 2026

The host teleprompter now has its own switch and works on a live webinar without switching on the interactive overlay. The reading surface for the host — the script, the beats, voice input and auto-scroll in the console tab and as a strip in the room — was only reachable together with the participant-facing interactive overlay. It now has its own gate, so a host can read his script while nothing about what participants see changes; the overlay keeps its own switch, exactly as before.

Voice input no longer dies quietly after a pause. When the browser ended a speech session on its own (a silence pause), the next start was called on the same recognition object — which the browser rejects, so the session stopped while the microphone button stayed green and nothing was transcribed. The recognizer is now rebuilt for every restart, and whatever was already transcribed is kept, so a pause costs nothing.

4.20.54 — 1 October 2026

Your webinar switch no longer takes the offer out of a room that is already open. Switching a live webinar off used to make the running room answer “this webinar is closed”, so participants who were sitting in it lost the offer until they reloaded. The room is already protected where it matters — nobody gets in without a valid registration or the host preview, and a participant link is bound to its own lead — and a real switch change still reaches the page through the switch poll. Nothing to configure.

Saving the offer while you are live simply saves it now. The “You are live right now” question in front of the save button is retired, because it asked about a risk that was measured away: the change is in the room about two seconds later, the cart always stays (it lives in the shop session, not in the frame), and only a half-filled checkout form can start over if the offer really has to be reloaded. The old wording is kept in the code for reference, not deleted.

A coupon that only the webinar window blocks now says so. When a webinar coupon is refused purely because the offer window is closed, the checkout used to answer with the shop’s generic “this coupon is not valid”. It now names the real reason — the coupon is valid during the webinar window. A coupon refused for any other reason keeps the shop’s own message; only the window is named, and only when nothing else has refused it first.

4.20.53 — 1 October 2026

The currency of your webinar is a field of the offer now, not a hidden payment setting. You set the currency your participants pay in right where the offers are built (the console’s offer panel), and every offer and its checkout link is built with it. Until now the value lived only in the payment-provider settings under a vendor-specific name (stripe_currency), which is how a webinar that sells in dollars could quietly carry a euro setting. An existing webinar keeps the value it already had; nothing has to be re-entered.

4.20.52 — 1 October 2026

Your registration page is centred again, on every template. The outer block of registration templates 1 and 2 was full width, so on a wide screen the card sat against the left edge while the video stayed in the middle (measured at 2560 px: card 2520 px, video 1360 px, 20 px at each edge). Both templates now use the same centred frame template 3 always had (measured: card 1300 px, 630 px margin on each side), and on phone and tablet the card matches that reference exactly — no sideways scrolling.

Your licence is active the moment the purchase goes through. After a purchase the plugin could keep its own cached licence for up to five minutes and still report “free” while the buyer was already looking at the dashboard. The cache is now cleared with the licence actions of the payment provider and at the end of the checkout return, so the plan is there when the buyer lands back. Nothing to configure.

Clicks are counted twice: everything that arrives, and what people really did. The existing counter adds up every request that reaches the site — measured on a test campaign, 30 clicks against 131 impressions, a rate no real room reaches, because bots and scanners (mail testers, curl, old browser strings) land there too, and because one visitor can account for several buttons. A second, stricter counter now records only real people: automated requests are kept out, and one visitor counts once. Nothing about the old number changes; the honest one sits next to it.

A dead offer link is now found by you, not by your participant. An evergreen webinar is opened by nobody, so a broken or un-framable offer URL would be discovered by the person who wants to buy. The CTA links are now checked when the link is pasted into the console — once per domain, not once per link, and only when an admin adds or changes one — and a link that does not answer or cannot be framed inside the offer costs one readiness point, the same weight a failed core check carries.

The salutation reaches your checkout. “Herr” or “Frau” is now carried through to the offer URL as its own value, so a provider that documents a salutation parameter can prefill it — including the case where the value comes from the lead or the WordPress profile and the two disagree, which is asked instead of guessed.

4.20.51 — 30 September 2026

The offer in your live room is one short card with three steps and two arrows. The offer no longer carries the trailing “related” block, the card itself is compact, and two arrows step through the offers of the campaign within the same frame — the page behind them never reloads and the cart stays as it is. The console panel next to it folds into sections, so the offer settings are reachable without scrolling past everything else.

4.20.50 — 30 September 2026

A registration page now uses the old hardcoded layout only when the webinar really is one of the old hardcoded (HC) webinars. On a modern webinar whose page was still marked as an old-style page, the registration view was built by the old layout without the styles it depends on (Bootstrap, Foundation, Font Awesome), so the form came out unstyled. The decision now follows the webinar’s type alone: a modern webinar renders its own page, an old hardcoded webinar keeps its layout exactly as before. Nothing to configure.

4.20.49 — 30 September 2026

A one-click registration now keeps the timezone of the person who clicked. The one-click link in your invitation emails registered a live-webinar guest on the server before their browser was ever asked — so every guest got the website’s timezone instead of their own, and on the attendee list they all looked identical (a guest in the UK showed the same zone as one in Panama, while someone who used the form showed their real zone). The browser now does the registration for live webinars, so each contact carries their own timezone; the campaign’s event timezone stays on the row for the thank-you page and the emails, exactly as before. If a browser cannot run the automatic sign-up, a one-click fallback still registers the guest — then with the website’s timezone, which is as much as can be known without a browser. The attendee list in the live console shows the guest’s own timezone as an extra line whenever it differs from the event.

4.20.48 — 30 September 2026

The “what’s next” bar now appears for every host, not only on our test site. The small host-only strip at the bottom — two tap rows, “On this page” and “Your next step”, that open the assistant and prefill a sample request — was held back to our staging site while the call-to-action deep link was still wrong. That link has been fixed since, and you have seen the strip on your own staging page, so it is released for everyone now. It stays host-only: visitors and participants never see it, because it needs a logged-in admin with the webinar dashboard capability.

4.20.47 — 30 September 2026

The AI Agent now shows your emails instead of only talking about them. When the agent offered “Check the emails”, clicking it answered in prose. It now shows the stored confirmation and reminder emails as clean, readable cards right in the chat — subject, heading, preview text and body. It is read-only: nothing is changed. The backend agent keeps what you typed. In the wp-admin agent, tapping a fallback chip such as “Hab ich unten geschrieben” while the box already held text sent only the chip’s label and cleared the box, so the agent asked the same question again. It now sends what you typed; with an empty box it just invites you to type.

4.20.39 — 29 September 2026

The AI Agent can now set the webinar language while importing an existing webinar. When a host migrated an older webinar and named a language (“make it an English webinar”), the agent answered “I could not do that, nothing changed. Reason: No capability exists yet for: language.” — the import tool had no language field at all, so the imported webinar silently kept the language of its source. The import now takes the language and the participant pages (registration, thank-you, live) come out in it. Nothing to configure; it works as soon as you update.

4.20.38 — 29 September 2026

Your webinar always speaks the language you gave it — no matter what language your WordPress site runs in. An English webinar on a German site started in German: the registration page, the thank-you page and the live room took the language of the page they sat on instead of the language of the campaign. The campaign’s own language now wins on every participant surface and in the reminder emails, in every language the plugin ships — a German webinar on an English site stays German as well. The AI Agent sends again. After something had been typed on the Create screen the composer could fall silent: the arrow appeared and typing worked, but every further message was only queued and never answered. The agent now notices a turn that never finished and releases it, so your next message goes out.

4.20.37 — 29 September 2026

The dashboard now says “Trial” while the trial is running — and stops calling it free. At the top of the WebinarIgnition dashboard the plan line read “Free” during an active trial instead of “ULTIMATE UNLIMITED PLUS (30 days trial)”, so a host in his trial saw the wrong state after a normal reload. The local licence read now carries the trial title like the online one, and it drops back to “Free” the moment the trial has run out. The logo colour now follows the licence, not the language: the paid logo used to be chosen by comparing the translated plan text to the English word “Free”, so on any non-English site a free account could show the customer logo and a paying one could lose it. The header now asks the licence itself, in every language.

4.20.34 — 29 September 2026

Your own test calls are counted separately again. A logged-in host is recognised on his own webinar pages again, so his own visits and test sign-ups go into a separate self-test bucket instead of the real numbers. The “Remove admin statistics” button clears that self-test activity in one click, so the chart shows only your real leads — handy at the start, when ten test calls would otherwise sit next to three real sign-ups. Real visitor rows and lead rows are never deleted.

4.20.30 — 28 September 2026

Registration, thank-you and live-room pages now recognize their shortcode in every page builder. If a builder such as Kubio saved the WebinarIgnition shortcode with escaped quotes, the page is read like a plain one again: participants see their own registration, thank-you and live-room pages, and the host’s image-edit buttons appear only on the participant surfaces — never on plugin logos or other images. Nothing to configure; it works as soon as you update.

4.20.22 — 27 September 2026

The registration animation never changes every page silently, and never overwrites your own edit. A webinar can render on several registration pages: animation texts without a named page now change nothing at all, the pages are listed instead, and the assistant asks “only this page or all of them?” before anything is written. A page whose animation you changed by hand is left exactly as it is and reported separately, and it is only replaced after a clear confirmation. Every report names the pages by title instead of just their number. A new host photo keeps your own lines: on a page you edited by hand only the portrait is swapped, every word stays as you wrote it — and a page left untouched is reported as untouched, never as changed.

4.20.14 — 25 September 2026

The registration animation’s benefit lines are always complete. Slide 1’s three outcome lines are no longer cut at a fixed word count, so a sentence never ends mid-thought. The AI writes short, complete one-line benefits and the builder keeps whole sentences; a longer line wraps onto a second line instead of ending half-way.

4.20.9 — 24 September 2026

The host task strip is now the way into the assistant. On registration, thank-you and room pages (staging hosts only) the open setup tasks appear as two swipeable pill rows — “On this page” and “Your next step”. Tapping a pill opens the Mini-Agent and pre-fills an example instruction; nothing is sent until the host presses send. Items already done or confirmed drop out, a task local to the current page outranks the general next step, and the email briefing leads the list. Collapsing the strip leaves a small icon by the Mini-Agent that brings it back.

4.20.8 — 24 September 2026

The Daily chip speaks the host’s language, and the offline copy matches the server. The click text of the “Daily.co” facts chip now comes from the server translations like the other video chips, and the short offline/frontend fallback now states — like the relay prompt — that creating the Daily room also trips the 100ms→Daily confirm guard.

4.20.7 — 24 September 2026

Creating the Daily room can no longer drop a 100ms room silently. The 100ms→Daily confirm guard also fires when the room is created through create-room (which sets the video source itself). Follow-up to 4.20.6; the readme changelog is now aligned with the plugin version, and the new Daily strings are in the translation template.

4.20.6 — 24 September 2026

Daily.co reaches every entry point of the assistant, and no 100ms room is dropped silently. The Daily.co room is now offered in the page-level and dashboard assistant prompts too (not only the shared base), an existing Daily webinar is read back as its own video source, and switching an active 100ms webinar onto Daily now hits the same confirm guard as switching it to an embed video.

  • Daily.co in every assistant surface. The page-level and dashboard prompts now connect a Daily room the same way as the base prompt — save the API key + domain install-wide, switch a webinar onto Daily, create its room, and explain the two values and where they live.
  • Daily campaigns are reported truthfully. An existing Daily webinar now reads back as its own video source (not as a generic embed), and the facts panel shows “Daily.co room” as its own option.
  • No silent loss of a 100ms room. Switching an active 100ms webinar onto Daily — via the video argument or via create-room — now hits the same confirm guard as the embed path: the first call is refused, and the switch happens only after the host confirms.

4.19.560 — 20 September 2026

Colours reach the whole site, and every value is checked before it is written. Changing the brand colours now also updates the active theme’s Site Editor palette (with the semantic shades kept on Twenty Twenty-Five), emails can be coloured on their own, and a new value gate refuses a wrong value with the expected shape instead of storing it.

  • The Site Editor colours follow. wi_update_colors writes the active block theme’s palette — background, text and the button — and on Twenty Twenty-Five keeps the semantic shades and text tokens. Say the colour, the whole website follows.
  • Emails can differ from the site. A new email target writes only the email template colours and switches “emails follow the site” off itself, so the written colours really take effect.
  • Every value is checked before it is written. A bad value (a wrong hex, an impossible number, a made-up field value) is refused once, up front, with the expected shape — nothing half-written.
  • Read before you write. wi_get_colors reports whether an email override is active and whether the site palette is writable at all; short links carry per-link stats; the Mini agent payload now carries the live-room CTAs.
  • Several short links in one call. One invitation call can create one link per source (e.g. 1 WhatsApp + 3 Telegram groups) instead of duplicating a shared channel.

4.19.559 — 19 September 2026

Correct dates, a keep-forever update check, and a learning log that arrives. The date preview shows the weekday again, “Check again” sees new releases, and the assistant’s learning book no longer drops entries silently.

  • Date preview shows the weekday again. The German default “D, j. F Y” rendered its weekday as a day number (“14, 14. September 2026”) in the admin preview and in the evergreen date dropdown. Weekday tokens now translate in one pass, so D is a weekday and l no longer grows an extra letter.
  • “Check again” finds new releases. The update check and the Plugins/updates screens now always load the real Freemius …

description:
Run live, automated, and evergreen webinars on WordPress — registration, reminders, and sales on your own site. Free unlimited webinars; WooCommerce checkout inside the room on Plus.

  • Unlimited live, automated, and evergreen webinars — free on WordPress.org
  • Unlimited attendees; AI wizard for registration pages and reminder emails (24 languages)
  • Registration forms anywhere — footer, sidebar, popup (shortcodes)
  • Automated reminder emails — confirmation through post-webinar follow-up
  • WooCommerce-ready — button CTA on Free; checkout inside the webinar room on Plus
  • Works with YouTube Live, Zoom, Vimeo, or your own stream — optional built-in live video on Plus
  • Per-webinar language, timezone, and date format
  • 30-day Plus trial inside the plugin — unlock leads, unlimited CTAs, and in-room checkout

Quick start: 13-video setup playlist · AI content wizard · live demo webinars below

Who is this for?

  • WooCommerce shop owners who want to sell during the webinar, not after everyone leaves
  • Course creators and coaches who need registration, reminders, and evergreen replays in one plugin
  • Agencies running multilingual campaigns for clients
  • EU/DACH hosts who need GDPR-friendly registration and streaming on their own WordPress site

How pricing works (no surprises)

Free runs forever — unlimited live, automated, and evergreen webinars with unlimited attendees, no time limit, no demo mode. There are no per-attendee fees and no seat tiers: your price never jumps because one webinar did unusually well. Other platforms lock you into a high monthly tier all year even if you only fill the room once.

Plus ($99/mo) is for when you want to sell inside the room (WooCommerce and other checkouts), need built-in live video, and unlock individual leads and automations. Same flat plugin price whether you host a small group or a packed session — you only pay for the streaming you actually use.

Free (install from WordPress.org)

For: test and run real webinars before you pay.

  • Unlimited live, automated, and evergreen webinars
  • Unlimited attendees — dashboard shows total sign-up count
  • AI content wizard — registration pages and reminder emails (24 languages)
  • One in-webinar action per event — polls, booking, or any WordPress shortcode
  • Registration forms anywhere — footer, sidebar, popup (shortcodes)
  • Automated reminder emails — fully customizable
  • Per-webinar language, timezone, and date format
  • WooCommerce button CTA — link to your shop (checkout opens in a new tab)
  • 30-day Plus trial available inside the plugin

Unlimited plan

For: solo creators who never want to hit limits.

All paid plans include unlimited registrations, attendees, webinar time, webinars, and in-webinar interactions — extend with any WordPress plugin (polls, forms, booking, …).

  • Everything in Free, plus unlimited in-webinar interactions per event
  • Individual lead details — name, email, attendance, custom fields
  • Send registration and attendance data to your CRM (ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp, KlickTipp, FluentCRM, and more)
  • Paid webinars — charge for access (WooCommerce, Stripe, PayPal, Digistore24)
  • Bulk lead import and export (CSV)
  • 1:1 consultant tech support

Plus plan

For: growing teams who want more sales from every webinar.

  • Everything in Unlimited, plus:
  • Webinar grid — visitors find live and evergreen offers fast
  • Built-in live video (100ms) — meet and stream in a focused room (up to 20,000 viewers)
  • External page CTAs inside the webinar — checkout or booking pages as live offers
  • WooCommerce checkout inside the webinar room — no redirect, sell while trust is warm
  • 1:1 technical done-for-you setup

Plus VIP plan

For: hands-on VIP support and email automation bundled.

  • Everything in Plus, plus:
  • 1:1 VIP technical support — direct line to an expert
  • VIP meetings — plan funnels and launches together
  • Groundhogg Pro (1 site) included — email automation on your server

See all plans: webinarignition.com/#pricing

Real hosts, real results

Melanie needed registration, reminders, and tracking connected on WordPress — not five plugins that do not talk to each other. Tom stopped selling on the landing page and filled live webinars instead; by the third session, trust did the selling. Bastian demoed leather craft live and opened WooCommerce checkout inside the room so buyers never lost momentum.

Felix ran a symposium, not a sales pitch.

Seven hours live — 19 May 2026, 10:00–17:00 CET.
German and English, with live translation and language switching inside the webinar room.
About 600 people registered. More than 100 questions asked and answered in two-way chat — directly in the room, not in a separate tool.

The stream ran through 3Q Video — GDPR/DSGVO-compliant hosting in Germany and Europe, not a US-only stack.
Registrations, calendar entries, and reminder emails: all on WebinarIgnition, on 14a.tv.

Same live room you already know — cleaned up and ready for large crowds.
During the event, our live-update service (hosted in Frankfurt) sends instant signals to every screen — a new CTA, a new question, your answer, a status change — so your WordPress site does not have to reload over and over.
All registrations, chat, and attendee data stay on your WordPress site, where your hosting already is. The helper does not store that data.
Available on every plan, including free.

New: AI Webinar Content Wizard

You probably don’t wake up in the morning excited to write registration copy and reminder emails.

The AI wizard is there for exactly that.
Answer three simple questions — what your webinar is about, who it is for, and what should happen afterwards.
From there, the wizard creates three registration page versions and four reminder emails in your language.

24 languages included. More on request. Best quality powered by AI.

You don’t lose control. You can read, adjust and translate every line.
But you never have to start from a blank page again.

Generate your first webinar content here

Step-by-step setup playlist (13 videos, AI in video 3): Watch on YouTube

Free: AI Connector (MCP)

Connect an AI assistant — Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other MCP-capable tools — to your WordPress site, and build webinars from that chat.

What you can do from the chat:

  • Ask whether WebinarIgnition fits and what it costs — “Does WebinarIgnition fit what I need? What does it cost, and which integrations does it support?”
  • Find a topic and create the webinar — “I run a dog school. Find a topic for my audience and write my webinar — title, invitation emails and registration page.”
  • Set up and change the webinar on your own WordPress — “Set up my webinar on https://my-site.com and move the start date to next Tuesday.”

The assistant can create and update webinars: registration pages, emails, dates, and settings. You read and edit every line afterwards, the same way as with the AI wizard above. What an assistant can do depends on the assistant and its plan.

It works on ordinary hosting, and it also works when your site cannot be reached from outside — behind a bot wall, a firewall, or shared hosting that blocks incoming requests. The site then reaches the connector itself and polls for work: no inbound access is needed, and nothing on your host has to change.

You find it under WebinarIgnition > AI connection (the same connection panel is on the Settings screen). Connecting needs an administrator account. Free on every plan.

Join a live demo webinar

  • Webinar Driver School (English): Beginner to pro — all welcome — Thursday 11:15 a.m. Panama time (UTC-5, 16:15 UTC)
  • WooCommerce Shop Owners: Triple Your WooCommerce Sales in 30 Minutes
  • WooCommerce Agencies: Stop starting every client project from zero
  • German (DE): Wednesday 18:30 Berlin time (CET)
  • Demo site: demo.webinarignition.com

Free Webinar Plugin for WooCommerce

Install from WordPress.org and run complete webinars before you pay — live, automated, and evergreen, with unlimited events and attendees. See the Free (install from WordPress.org) plan block above for the full list.

Start free, run a few webinars, and upgrade when you need individual lead details, unlimited in-room actions, CRM handoff, or WooCommerce checkout inside the room. Plans: webinarignition.com/#pricing

Paid Plans: WooCommerce Shops, Agencies & Creators

See the Unlimited, Plus, and Plus VIP plan blocks at the top of this page for the full feature list. All paid plans include unlimited registrations, attendees, webinar time, webinars, and in-webinar interactions.

See all plans: webinarignition.com/#pricing

What Only WebinarIgnition Does

  • WooCommerce checkout embedded inside the webinar room — no redirect, auto-fill customer data, sell while the feeling is warm (Plus)
  • AI-generated registration pages + reminder emails — 3 pages, 4 emails, 24 languages, in minutes (free on all plans)
  • Registration shortcodes anywhere, unlimited times — footer, sidebar, popup, any page
  • Per-webinar language, timezone, and date format — your attendees register and buy in their native language
  • 24 languages out of the box — every language on request, best quality by AI
  • Recurring live webinars + re-invite all registered with one click
  • 1-click registration from email — attendees click once, instantly registered, no form fill
  • Custom registration fields auto-filled in CTAs and CRM handoff (paid plans)
  • 100ms live video — up to 20,000 participants (Plus)
  • All webinar types in one plugin — live, automated, evergreen, no add-ons needed
  • No attendee limits on any plan

WooCommerce Integration

  • Free: Add a button CTA linking to your WooCommerce product page — keep the connection warm, send them to the shop when the moment is right
  • Plus: Embed WooCommerce checkout directly inside the webinar room — products, subscriptions, upsells without a page redirect, while trust is at its peak
  • Auto-fill checkout forms with data from webinar registration (name, email, address for logged-in customers)
  • Sell WooCommerce subscriptions, memberships, and courses inside webinars
  • Integrate with CartFlows, FunnelKit, and WPFunnels for complete funnel automation
  • Send registration and attendance data (name, email, campaign tags, attended status, product purchased) to your CRM

Integrations

  • Email & CRM: ActiveCampaign, Mailchimp, Mautic, KlickTipp, FluentCRM, Groundhogg, Brevo — via webhooks or direct
  • Payments: WooCommerce, Digistore24, Stripe, PayPal
  • Upsell funnels: CartFlows, FunnelKit, WPFunnels
  • Video: YouTube Live, Zoom, Vimeo, your own live stream, MP4/video files, iframe embeds; built-in live video (100ms) on Plus
  • Social login: Nextend Social Login (22+ providers, external, free or ~$50)
  • Page builders: Elementor, Gutenberg/FSE, Divi, Beaver Builder, Thrive Architect, Oxygen, Bricks

Multilingual Webinars — 24 Languages

Your webinar works best when people can follow every line without effort.
Reading and listening in a second language always costs energy — and every bit of extra effort lowers conversion.

Each webinar runs in its own language, timezone and date format.
Registration page, emails, thank-you page and the webinar room itself adapt to the audience you choose.

24 languages out of the box. Every language on request. Best quality powered by AI.

Hand-translated: English (en_US), German (de_DE)
AI-translated: Spanish (es_ES, es_MX), French (fr_FR), Italian (it_IT), Dutch (nl_NL), Portuguese (pt_BR, pt_PT), Russian (ru_RU), Chinese (zh_CN), Hindi (hi_IN), Turkish (tr_TR), Ukrainian (uk), Hungarian (hu_HU), Croatian (hr), Japanese (ja), Urdu (ur), Bulgarian (bg), Romanian (ro)

Add or refine translations with the free Loco Translate plugin (auto-translate via DeepL, Microsoft, ChatGPT built in).

GDPR & Privacy

All registration and attendee data stays on your own server. Double opt-in is required before any contact is saved as a participant. Forms include consent fields and compliance options for EU/DACH. No participant data is sent to external services without your explicit configuration.
